analysis.evidence: Abram takes Sarai, already identified as his wife, along with Lot, their possessions, and the people they had acquired in Haran. The next verb, וַיֵּצְאוּ (‘and they set out’), shows that Abram took them with him on the journey to Canaan.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Abram as its subject.

draft.change: Clear the unsupported root אבה and its link to article 2bh. Preserve the explanation of the compound name and its recorded bearer.
draft.definition: Abram, the earlier name of Abraham, son of Terah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:26 identifies Abram as Terah’s son, and Genesis 17:5 records his change of name. The first element of אַבְרָם is the noun אָב, “father.” Neither verse supports deriving the name from אָבָה, “be willing.”

analysis.evidence: אַבְרָם is the subject of וַיִּקַּח, “he took.” The verse identifies Sarai as his wife and Lot as his brother’s son.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham

analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.
